preconditions.description: Grid dimensions n and m are integers between 1 and 100 inclusive, with total squares at least 2.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is a non-negative integer k, representing the minimum number of teleporters.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.splitlines()) == k + 1 + n * m and all(line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip())
postconditions.description: Output consists of k teleporter lines followed by n*m+1 path lines, with no empty lines.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 4 for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:k+1]) and all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= m for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:k+1] for x, y in [(line.split()[0], line.split()[1]), (line.split()[2], line.split()[3])])
postconditions.description: Each teleporter line contains four integers (x1, y1, x2, y2) where coordinates are within grid bounds.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout.splitlines()[k+1:]) and all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= m for line in stdout.splitlines()[k+1:] for x, y in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: Each path line contains two integers (x, y) representing valid grid coordinates.

postconditions.expression: path := [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[k+1:]] and path[0] == (1, 1) and path[-1] == (1, 1)
postconditions.description: The path starts and ends at the capital (1, 1).
The path visits every square except the capital exactly once, and the capital exactly twice (start and end).

postconditions.expression: all(abs(path[i][0] - path[i+1][0]) + abs(path[i][1] - path[i+1][1]) <= 1 or any((path[i][0], path[i][1]) == (x1, y1) and (path[i+1][0], path[i+1][1]) == (x2, y2) for x1, y1, x2, y2 in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:k+1]]) for i in range(len(path)-1))
postconditions.description: The king moves only to side-neighboring squares or uses teleporters as defined.
